brand.title: IQVIA (Production)
brand.subtitle: Knowledge Check — IQVIA Predictive Clinical Development Messaging

questions.question: According to the course, what was the composite median R&D program duration in 2025?
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—the course cites Citeline Pharmapremia and the IQVIA Institute's February 2026 report showing growth from 8 years in 2016 to 10 years in 2025.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The data comes from the February 2026 report, which shows the 2025 composite median had grown to 10 years. This is the burning platform that grounds the entire value proposition.

questions.question: What is the maximum timeline acceleration IQVIA Predictive Clinical Development can deliver on a 10-year program?
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right—the headline claim is 'up to two years,' and this qualifier is essential to how you present it accurately in any sponsor meeting.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course emphasizes the precise language: 'up to two years,' not guaranteed or minimum. Every word in that sentence matters when you present it to sponsors.

questions.question: How many weeks does the Early Engagement framework typically run?
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—Early Engagement is structured as an 11-to-12-week engagement that produces four concrete artifacts the sponsor walks away with.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Early Engagement is designed as a time-bounded 11-to-12-week engagement, not longer. This specificity is what makes it work as a concrete close in a first conversation.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four concrete artifacts a sponsor receives from Early Engagement?
questions.feedback_correct: Right—the four Early Engagement deliverables are feasibility view, endpoint tradeoff matrix, country scenario models, and risk register; the Clinical Study Report comes much later.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The Clinical Study Report is a late-stage deliverable that comes after database lock. Early Engagement produces four specific artifacts that are ready within 11-12 weeks.

questions.question: What percentage faster is site contract negotiation and finalization under IQVIA's optimized approach?
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—site contract negotiation is 18 percent faster (9 weeks versus 11 weeks), and you should cite 'all figures are feasible under assumptions defined in the accelerated offerings' when mentioning these metrics.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Site contract negotiation is 18 percent faster (reducing from 11 weeks to 9 weeks). Remember to apply the qualifier about feasible assumptions whenever you cite these specific metrics in a sponsor conversation.

questions.question: According to the course, what is the typical consequence when a sponsor cannot meet the six qualification requirements?
choices: The timeline should still be guaranteed
The accelerated timeline outcomes are not achievable and should not be represented as if they are
The solution should be sold anyway with disclaimers
Early Engagement should be expanded to 16 weeks
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right—qualifying sponsor readiness is both a commercial and ethical responsibility; if the six requirements cannot be met, the accelerated outcomes are not achievable.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Sponsor readiness qualification is not just a process step—it is an ethical boundary that protects both the sponsor and IQVIA's credibility. If the requirements cannot be met, the timeline claims are not defensible.

questions.question: In a sponsor conversation about enrollment delays, which proof points should you prioritize selecting?
choices: All available proof points to show comprehensive capability
Two or three proof points that specifically match their enrollment pain
Only the AI tools in development
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—the discipline is in selecting two or three proof points that match the sponsor's specific pain, not leading with all of them at once.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course emphasizes selective proof-pointing; a sponsor worried about enrollment delays needs enrollment-specific proof points like first participant screened 18% faster or screen failure reduction, not generic metrics.

questions.question: According to the conversational sequence taught in this course, what is the second element after opening with the burning platform?
choices: Introduce the solution at headline level
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—the sequence is: burning platform, then pivot to revenue math (development time becomes commercial time and what two years is worth), then introduce the solution.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The revenue math pivot comes second, before the solution introduction. This order is intentional—you establish the problem and the value before presenting the mechanism for solving it.

questions.question: Which statement correctly reflects what IQVIA is claiming versus what it is NOT claiming about Predictive Clinical Development?
choices: IQVIA guarantees two years will be saved on every program
IQVIA can replace sponsor in-house capabilities, especially for Large Pharma
Up to two years is possible based on analyses and adoption of recommended approaches, but it is not guaranteed and the solution supplements rather than replaces in-house teams
AI tools in development can be sold as current capabilities if the sponsor asks
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—you've identified the three critical boundaries: not a guarantee, not a replacement (especially for Large Pharma), and in-development tools are never sold as current deliverables.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course establishes firm boundaries: the solution uses qualifiers ('up to two years'), supplements in-house capabilities rather than replacing them, and never sells in-development tools as current. Staying inside these boundaries protects both credibility and the relationship.

questions.question: In the capstone 90-second pitch, on what three dimensions does your voice instructor provide feedback?
choices: Speed of delivery, volume of metrics cited, and competitor comparison
Accuracy of headline claim and disclaimer, correct persona identification and tailoring, and Early Engagement as concrete next step
Slide recall, memorization of all four phases, and revenue math calculation
Cost justification, technology features, and site network size
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right—your instructor evaluates the accuracy of your headline claim and disclaimer, whether you correctly identified and tailored to the sponsor persona, and whether Early Engagement is presented as the concrete next step.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The three evaluation dimensions focus on accuracy (disclaimer included), persona fit (tailoring to their context), and a specific next step (Early Engagement), not on general recall or feature volume.
